findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext discards recorded logs, making log assertions useless
findings.body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns a brand new `TestLogger` instead of `f` (or a logger that writes back into `f`'s `Logs` fields). After this PR `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, so any test that injects a `TestLogger` into `NewLoggerMiddleware` and then asserts on `InfoLogs.Calls`/`Message`/`Ctx` will always see zero calls, even though the code logged. This silently removes the ability to unit-test the plugin request logging (and any other code path that uses `FromContext`). It should return the same instance (or a child that records into the parent's slices).

findings.title: ContextualLoggerMiddleware dereferences req without nil check
findings.body: `QueryData`, `CallResource`, `CheckHealth` and `CollectMetrics` access `req.PluginContext` unconditionally. `LoggerMiddleware` in the same package explicitly guards with `if req == nil { return m.next.X(...) }`, which indicates nil requests do reach the middleware chain (at minimum in tests). With this new middleware always inserted into the chain in `CreateMiddlewares`, a nil request now panics with a nil-pointer dereference instead of being forwarded. Add the same nil guards for consistency and safety.

findings.title: LoggerMiddleware silently loses pluginId/endpoint/dsName/uname unless ContextualLoggerMiddleware runs before it
findings.body: The log parameters `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `uname`, `dsName`, `dsUID` were removed from `logRequest` and are now expected to come from the contextual logger installed by the new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware`. This creates an undocumented ordering dependency: if `NewLoggerMiddleware` is used without `NewContextualLoggerMiddleware`, or the latter is registered after it in the chain (e.g. other call sites building their own middleware list, Enterprise code, or tests), the "Plugin Request Completed" egress log silently degrades to status/duration only, breaking log-based dashboards/alerts on these fields. At minimum document the requirement on both middlewares (the old `InstrumentationMiddleware` carried a "should live at the top of the middleware stack" comment, which was dropped), and ideally add a test asserting the egress log contains the plugin fields.

findings.title: Explicit traceID log field removed; now depends on a globally registered contextual provider
findings.body: The explicit `traceID` log parameter (previously added via `tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)`) was deleted from `logRequest`. The field now only appears if a contextual log provider that injects the trace ID has been registered globally with `pkg/infra/log`. In setups/tests where the tracing service (and therefore that provider) is not initialized, the `traceID` field disappears from the `grafana-data-egress` log line, breaking correlation between egress logs and traces. Verify the provider is always registered, or re-add the field explicitly.

findings.title: No test coverage for the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware
findings.body: The PR extracts contextual-logging behaviour into a new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` and makes `LoggerMiddleware` depend on it, but no test is added for either. Nothing verifies that `endpoint`, `pluginId`, `dsName`, `dsUID` and `uname` end up in the context (and thus in the egress log line), so a future regression in this middleware or in middleware ordering would go unnoticed. Also, the renamed test still declares `func TestInstrumentationMiddleware`, which no longer matches the `MetricsMiddleware` name it exercises.

findings.title: Adding FromContext to the Logger interface breaks all existing implementors
findings.body: `FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger` is added to the `plugins/log.Logger` interface. Every type implementing this interface must now provide the method; only `grafanaInfraLogWrapper` and `TestLogger` are updated in this PR. Any other implementation in the repository (fakes/mocks in other packages, embedded wrappers) will fail to compile, and out-of-tree implementations break. Confirm there are no other implementors, or provide an embeddable base/no-op implementation.
